ml_introduction.objective: Understand what machine learning is, the difference between supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, and common real-world applications.

data_preprocessing.objective: Apply data cleaning, normalization, standardization, and handling of missing values to prepare datasets for ML models.

linear_regression.objective: Understand and implement linear regression, interpret coefficients, and evaluate model fit using MSE and R-squared.

logistic_regression.objective: Apply logistic regression for binary classification, interpret sigmoid output as probability, and evaluate with accuracy and confusion matrix.

decision_trees.objective: Build and interpret decision trees, understand splitting criteria (Gini, entropy), and control overfitting via max depth.

model_evaluation.objective: Apply train/test split and k-fold cross-validation; compute precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC.

overfitting_regularization.objective: Identify overfitting and underfitting; apply L1/L2 regularization and understand the bias-variance tradeoff.

ensemble_methods.objective: Understand bagging, boosting, and Random Forests; explain how ensembles reduce variance and bias.

clustering.objective: Apply k-means and hierarchical clustering; choose k using the elbow method and interpret cluster assignments.

neural_network_basics.objective: Describe the structure of a feedforward neural network, explain forward propagation, activation functions, and gradient descent.

notes: 10-topic ML Basics domain for the curric-agents pilot study.
